headline: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra runs on Nvidia's RTX Spark chip
dek: The laptop starts at $2,599 and runs AI models on the device, not in the cloud (CNBC, The Verge).

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A laptop built around an Nvidia chip
body: Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra on Wednesday at an event in San Francisco. It is its first laptop built around Nvidia's RTX Spark chip, starting at $2,599 and shipping October 16 (CNBC, The Verge).

The laptop has a 15-inch touchscreen with up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness and HDR support (CNBC, The Verge, Engadget, Hipertextual). It weighs about 4.4 pounds, roughly 2 kilograms (CNBC, Engadget).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: AI that runs on the device
s3.body: RTX Spark is an Arm-based chip designed to run AI models directly on the laptop instead of sending the work to the cloud (CNBC, The Verge, Hipertextual).

points.t: 24GB of unified memory, one pool shared by processor and graphics chip, rising to 128GB on higher-end models (CNBC, The Verge).
A magnetic USB-C port detaches if someone trips on the cable, similar to Apple's MagSafe (CNBC, The Verge).
Windows 11 Execution Containers isolate AI agents to block unwanted access to the rest of the system (CNBC, TechCrunch).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A bid for developers' desks
body: Microsoft and Nvidia are placing RTX Spark laptops at the premium end of the market, aimed at creative software, gaming and local AI work (Engadget).
Microsoft is offering up to $1,000 off to buyers who trade in a MacBook Pro, aiming at developers who favor Apple's computers for AI and coding work (TechCrunch).

items.t: The Surface Laptop Ultra ships; the top-end version had already sold out in the US on launch day (TechCrunch).
The Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a developer mini PC with the same chip, ships starting at $5,999 (The Verge, TechCrunch).
Meta is bringing a Windows version of its Muse AI agent, currently available only on Mac (CNBC, The Verge).

caption.hook: Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra, its first laptop built around Nvidia's RTX Spark chip, at $2,599.
body: Pricing climbs with memory: Hipertextual listed a 64GB configuration at $4,699. Dell also revealed its XPS 16 Creator Edition with the same Nvidia chip, priced at $3,800, according to TechCrunch.

It is not Microsoft's first push to tie hardware to AI. In 2024 it introduced the Copilot+ PC standard, which required a dedicated AI chip (CNBC). A new Windows feature, Hybrid Intelligence, lets Copilot use files stored on the PC to carry out tasks, according to The Verge and Engadget.
caption.cta: For local AI work, which matters more in a laptop like this: memory, price or the chip itself?
